title: Daily engine checks on a sailing yacht
lead: Most engine trouble on a charter yacht shows up in a five-minute check before you start. Here is what to look at, what to watch while the engine runs and what to do when an alarm goes off.
description: Daily diesel checks on a sailing yacht: oil, coolant, raw water strainer, belt, bilge and fuel, starting and the exhaust water, gauges and alarms, fuel range and common faults.
summary: Check the oil, coolant, raw water strainer, belt, bilge and fuel filter every morning, with the engine cold.
Start in neutral and look over the stern: cooling water must come out of the exhaust within a few seconds.
A temperature or oil pressure alarm means neutral, then stop the engine as soon as the boat is safe.
Never switch the batteries off while the engine runs, and plan fuel so a quarter of the tank is left on arrival.
